corroboration.role: Community gameplay corroboration, not native executable proof
facts: Talent note: own discount expires after first successful deployment; retreat discount applies to all ordinary cards until any affected operator deploys, then expires globally.
Charger refund is capped by the smaller of actual deployment expenditure and original potential-adjusted cost; first-deploy reductions are excluded from the original cost.

runtimeMapping.cost: Own runtime_cost only on first successful spawn; flat talent additions after the existing ordinary redeploy calculation; next-operator discount shared across ordinary cards and consumed atomically once. Tokens and cancelled/failed placements do not consume. Refund min(lastCost, raw potential-adjusted cost).
runtimeMapping.normal: Original Attack event .333 at playback capped at1, one ground target, ordinary block priority.
runtimeMapping.s1: Selected two physical hits, first original Skill_1 event .333 then explicit MultiMelee triggerDelta .25 divided by capped playback. No target replacement between hits. Extra DP only for the S1 hit which kills. Lost target before first strike refunds one charge; controls/owner departure cancel remaining strikes. SP blocked through this attack sequence.
runtimeMapping.s2: Source passive selected duration/ATK/DEF/block+1 on each deployment. Original Start_2/Skill_2_Idle/Skill_2_Loop (Down variant only on Front)/Skill_2_End. Self selector maps to ordinary block-priority target selection limited by current block capacity; no splash, no extra targets outside this cap.

verificationLimits: Original tables, graphs, buff templates, facing byte hashes and all20skill-rank records retained. PRTS notes corroborate card/refund interpretation; the native C# dispatcher and integer composition are not recovered.

S1 explicit triggerDelta uses animation playback rate; second literal .5 event is not used because waitAttackEventForAllAttacks is false. Cast completion/target-dead refund and control ordering are reviewed simulator policies, not frame parity.
S2 numeric selector/mode/FSM dispatcher is mapped to ordinary source-supported block priority and target cap. Deployment-protection quirks and Unity particles are not reproduced.
No module is enabled by this kit.
